---
title: "Can we make optimisation more efficient by building a lookup table for the airfoil?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# The same design solve twice, differing only in where the section polar comes
# from. The table's design is then re-trimmed through the exact network, which
# is the only way to ask whether its answer was real.
table = section_table()

t0 = time.perf_counter(); exact = optimise()
t_exact = time.perf_counter() - t0
t0 = time.perf_counter(); cached = optimise(table=table)
t_cached = time.perf_counter() - t0

DESIGN = ("aspect_ratio", "tail_arm_chords", "h_tail_ratio", "h_tail_incidence")
flown = glide(*glider(span=0.30, **{k: cached[k] for k in DESIGN}),
              static_margin=0.10)

speedup = t_exact / t_cached
penalty = flown["sink"] / exact["sink"] - 1
payback = table["seconds"] / (t_exact - t_cached)
cl_err = section_error(table)

assert speedup > 1                      # the table is faster, or there is no question
assert payback < 2                      # and pays for itself inside two solves
assert cl_err < 0.02                    # the section really is well fitted
assert penalty > 0.1                    # yet the design it picks is much worse
```

::: {.hero-pair}
::: {.hero-ref}
[`{python} f"{speedup:.1f}"`×]{.hero-value}
[faster per solve]{.hero-label}
:::
::: {}
[`{python} f"{penalty:.0%}"`]{.hero-value}
[worse, once flown exactly]{.hero-label}
:::
:::

**Answer.** Yes, and it does not help. Fitting the table costs
`{python} f"{table['seconds']:.1f}"` s and repays inside
`{python} f"{payback:.1f}"` solves. But the optimiser then walks into the
table's own error: it claims `{python} f"{cached['sink']:.4f}"` m/s at aspect
ratio `{python} f"{cached['aspect_ratio']:.1f}"`, and that aircraft flown
through the network sinks at [`{python} f"{flown['sink']:.4f}"`]{.key}
(@tbl-cost). Worst CL error in the table is only
`{python} f"{cl_err:.3f}"`: the section is barely wrong, and the design badly
so.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A small section error is not a small design error
An optimiser will find wherever the surrogate is most wrong, and stop there.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **One start** per solve; the surface has basins.
2. **Static margin 10%**, as chapter 01.
3. **Error sampled at midpoints**, where a spline is worst.
:::

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cost
#| tbl-cap: "The same design solve, differing only in where the section polar is read from. The last row re-trims each design through the exact network, so both are judged by the same aerodynamics rather than each by its own."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
md_table(["", "network", "table"], [
    ("solve, s", f"{t_exact:.1f}", f"{t_cached:.1f}"),
    ("aspect ratio", f"{exact['aspect_ratio']:.2f}", f"{cached['aspect_ratio']:.2f}"),
    ("sink claimed, m/s", f"{exact['sink']:.4f}", f"{cached['sink']:.4f}"),
    ("sink as flown, m/s", f"{exact['sink']:.4f}", f"{flown['sink']:.4f}"),
])
```
